Protein Food

Pork Chop

About This Entry

Pork chops are cross-cuts from the loin with a mild, slightly sweet pork flavor. Bone-in chops retain more moisture; both suit Pinot Gris, unoaked Chardonnay, and soft reds.

Beginner Guide

Thicker bone-in rib chops have more flavor than thin loin chops. Brining helps prevent dryness on the grill.

Wine Pairing Explanation

Primary wine styles

  • pinot noir

Alternative wine styles

  • chardonnay

FAQ

What is Pork Chop?
Thicker bone-in rib chops have more flavor than thin loin chops.
How should Pork Chop be cooked?
Cook to safe internal temperature; richer cuts tolerate slow cooking, smoke, and braising that build pairing-friendly flavor.
